goal: Implement the reviewed Astrology UX updates and package them as a new internal Android QA build without changing chart calculation, schema, or app data.
successCriteria: A first-time reviewer can find Sun, Moon, Rising, and a house from Chart Story without switching to another tab to discover the controls.
The zodiac lens card has readable bilingual text at the approved mobile viewport and meets the brand contrast target.
The Guide composer is visible in its focus/full state, preserves keyboard and safe-area room, and suggested questions change with the selected focus.
Free users see an honest locked Premium state before consent or submission, while the server remains the final entitlement authority.
Generic loading no longer replays the welcome brand reveal, and native splash behavior remains safe for offline and session-recovery failure paths.
Create an internal Android QA APK from current reviewed mobile source, with a distinct version and SHA-256 manifest.
Install using replacement install only, preserve existing app data, and confirm package version plus successful cold launch.
The build workaround redirects only Expo Dev Launcher Gradle generated outputs to the workspace cache and leaves dependency sources untouched.
untouchedSurfaces: Astrology chart calculation, timezone and birth-data contracts remain unchanged.
Supabase migrations, Edge Function deployment, provider credentials, payment SKUs, and entitlement tables remain unchanged.
Admin Content Operations and AI Studio remain unchanged; no raw birth data or journal data is added to telemetry.
Tarot, Persona, Journal, Profile, public Help, and brand asset source files remain unchanged.

impact.entryPoint: Explore or saved Astrology chart opens Chart Story; Guide remains a tab inside the chart sheet and the app startup path remains AccountBoundary to AccountApp.
impact.dataWrite: Only transient chart selection and question presentation state change; no new birth-data, journal, AsyncStorage, or database write is introduced.
impact.backendContract: The existing Astrology AI request/response contract is consumed more completely for suggested follow-ups; entitlement and quota remain server-owned and no migration or deploy is performed.
impact.adminVisibility: No new admin data is exposed; existing AI trace and sanitized report behavior remains the operator view.
impact.privacySafety: The Guide continues sending only calculated fact IDs and the current consented question; locked-state messaging prevents a free user from entering consent before entitlement is known.
impact.observability: No sensitive analytics are added; existing error and usage paths remain, with local QA focused on startup milestones and chart selection discoverability.
impact.rollback: Revert the scoped mobile files; the existing chart, local fallback, locked Guide, and welcome flow remain available. Backend behavior is unchanged.

canonicalContracts: packages/agent-config/astrology-ai-insight/response.schema.json is the canonical Astrology AI response contract.
apps/mobile/src/features/astrology/astrologyAiInsight.ts is the mobile adapter for that contract.
The server entitlement check in supabase/functions/ai-astrology-insight remains authoritative.

securityReview.authzRls: No auth or RLS code is changed; the client lock is only a UX guard and the server entitlement check remains authoritative.
securityReview.sensitiveData: Birth details, coordinates, journal, chat history, and raw account identifiers stay outside the new UI state and request payload.
securityReview.secretsLogging: No credentials, provider keys, or raw personal content are added to code, logs, or the plan.
securityReview.externalInput: User questions remain sanitized and consent-gated by the existing adapter; suggested labels are rendered as text only.
securityReview.dependencies: No dependency version or source changes. A Gradle init script redirects only Expo Dev Launcher generated outputs to the workspace cache, and Kotlin compilation runs in-process to avoid daemon session writes under the restricted dependency directory.
securityReview.migrationRelease: No migration, database push, Edge Function deploy, payment release, or store release is performed. The local Android release APK is debug-signed for internal QA and is installed with adb install -r only; never uninstall or clear app data.
securityReview.stopCondition: Stop if the mobile check, targeted tests, preflight, or device review shows a regression in account isolation, consent, or chart selection.

workingTreeReview.note: These mobile and Astrology paths already contain owner-supplied uncommitted A3/A4 work; the implementation is constrained to the reviewed files and preserves unrelated changes. A prior native build hit an access-denied Gradle-generated output under node_modules; the retry writes that output to the task-local cache. The init script was reviewed and only redirects one dependency Gradle output into the workspace cache.

validationCommands: Manual Android path: cold start → Explore → Astrology → open saved chart → find Moon, Rising, House 7 → open Guide → verify locked Free state and composer visibility.
Manual Android path: warm reopen and offline/session-recovery smoke check without clearing account data.
Gradle :app:assembleRelease for arm64-v8a using the workspace-local Gradle caches
adb shell dumpsys package app.nilaza.mobile (verify installed versionName/versionCode)
adb shell monkey -p app.nilaza.mobile 1 (cold-launch smoke check)
Gradle Kotlin compiler uses in-process execution to avoid writing daemon session files under node_modules
managerTestPath: On the connected Air1 Ultra, confirm app version 0.1.3/build 4 and cold launch. Then open Astrology from Explore, create or open a chart, use the visible story selector to read Moon/Rising/House 7, inspect the readable zodiac lens, open Guide and verify the question field stays visible above the keyboard and Free users see Premium status before consent. Do not send a new AI request unless the user reviews and accepts fresh in-app consent.
residualRisk: Native splash P95 across offline, expired-session, and low-end devices still needs a release-build matrix; this APK remains internal QA signed with the debug key and Mobile Quality CI has not run on a pushed commit. AI success and quota retrieval remain backend/staging gates; this install does not send an AI request.
